title: Lowering bug: Expr::Cast drops parens around a binary inner operand in spec position — (n-1) as nat lowers to n - 1 as nat = n - (1 as nat) (Verus precedence) -> int/nat mismatch L0

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Root cause: `as` binds tighter than the binary/unary operators in both Verus and Rust, but every cast-emit site in the lowering used a bare format!("{inner} as {ty}") / format!("{lowered} as usize"). A cast over a binary inner thus mis-binds: (n-1) as nat -> n - 1 as nat = n - (1 as nat) (int/nat mismatch, L0); (i-1) as usize -> i - (1 as usize) (u64-usize, E0277). Fix the CAUSE for the whole class: parenthesize the inner ONLY when it is an Expr::Binary/Unary (a simple inner never mis-binds, so corpus/golden simple casts stay byte-identical — no regression). Sites fixed in lower.rs + l1.rs: the Expr::Cast arm, the byte_at/slice 'as usize' coercion, the split 'as u8' coercion, and lower_index_arg's combinator 'as int'. Authority: tests/golden/lower/parse_u64.verus.rs (hand-authored) already writes the paren'd form '(k - 1) as nat' / '(s.len() - 1) as int'.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Fixed in 8d86189. Parenthesized the cast inner ONLY for an Expr::Binary/Unary inner across the whole class of cast-emit sites in thermite-lower/src/lower.rs + l1.rs: the Expr::Cast arm (both files), the byte_at/slice 'as usize' index coercion (both), the split 'as u8' separator coercion (both), and lower_index_arg's combinator 'as int' (lower.rs). A simple inner is left unparenthesized so the corpus/golden simple casts (i as int, acc as nat, 0 as usize) stay byte-identical. Verified against real verus 0.2026.05.24: (k-1) as nat spec fn -> L3; byte_at(i-1) in a contract -> L3 (11 obligations, no u64/usize mismatch); forge build of byte_at(i-1) -> L1 built. Added regression pin thermite-lower/tests/divergence_cast_paren.rs (4/4). Gauntlet: cargo test --workspace 667 passed/0 failed; clippy -D warnings PASS; fmt --check PASS.
